ep04.c01.tear: Tear it up. Pay the price.
ep04.c01.prompt: The pen is in your hand
ep04.o02: The paper tore in two. The commissioner sighed and put the handcuffs on the table.
ep04.o01: Karaliman forgets one thing: dates. It never forgets one thing: names.
ep05.title: Ending: The Silent Table
ep05.l01: All three are at the table. Nobody speaks. They don't need to.
ep05.l02: Each of them carries a secret. Each of them knows the others'.
ep05.l03: The hand that signed off the fault. The hand that took the envelope. The hand that deleted the recording. At the same table, reaching for the same bread.
journal.ep05.ep05_photo: Three people are laughing in the photo. None of them remembers that day.
ep05.it.ep05_photo.l1: All three are laughing in the photo. Nobody remembers what happened that day.
ep05.it.ep05_radio.l1: News on the radio: 'The cause of the Karaliman fire remains unknown.' Someone switches it off.
ep05.x01.objective: Sit at the table. Keep or break the silence when ready.
ep05.c01.hand: Put your hand on the table, next to theirs.
ep05.o02: A mouth opened. Across the table, a small nod: I know. The sentence was never finished.
ep05.o01: The silence wasn't a lie. It was a contract. And all three had signed it.
ch01.it.ch01_thermos.l1: A thermos left on the bench. Felt pen on the lid: 'SELIM — DON'T TOUCH'.
ch01.it.ch01_thermos.l2: Ten years, same thermos. Does he still take his tea without sugar?
ch01.it.ch01_thermos.l3: If the new arm had a thermos, would they write its name on it too?
journal.ch01.ch01_mirror: Kemal, 41. Twenty years on the maintenance crew. Raised Defne on his own.
ch01.it.ch01_mirror.l1: A forty-one-year-old man in a cracked mirror. The rings under his eyes map every night shift.
ch01.it.ch01_mirror.l2: Defne says the helmet leaves a mark even after I take it off. She's right.
ch01.it.ch01_mirror.l3: Last check today. If the line opens tomorrow, maybe no more night shifts. Maybe no shifts at all.
ch01.it.ch01_conveyor.l1: The belt is set to the new arm's pace. Not to a person's.
ch01.it.ch01_conveyor.l2: Six people worked this belt last year. They've left room for two.
ch01.it.ch01_conveyor.l3: Nobody asked us. If they had, we'd have told them: people get tired. Machines don't, but they break.
journal.ch01.ch01_tea: Riza started here as an apprentice; Kemal brought him from the neighbourhood. Later he moved to the port and a truck.
ch01.it.ch01_tea.l1: The kettle is boiling. A faded photo on the wall: the plant's twentieth year, a grinning apprentice in front.
ch01.it.ch01_tea.l2: Riza. He was nineteen. I brought him from the neighbourhood. He learned welding here before the truck.
ch01.it.ch01_tea.l3: Someone has written under the photo in ballpoint: 'We built this factory.'
journal.ch01.ch01_nevin_talk: Nevin, production chief. Says the list came 'from above'. She is afraid of being on the next one.
ch01.it.ch01_nevin_talk.l1: Don't look at me like that, Kemal. I didn't write the list. They only gave me a number.
ch01.it.ch01_nevin_talk.l3: Twelve. I was to find the names. I'm a number too, just a little higher up the list.
ch01.it.ch01_nevin_talk.l4: If the line doesn't open tomorrow, I'm on the next list. Know that too.
ch02.it.ch02_thermos.l1: A tea urn boils in the strike tent. Someone presses a plastic cup into Defne's hand.
ch02.it.ch02_thermos.l2: Thanks. These cups get thinner every year, have you noticed?
ch02.it.ch02_thermos.l3: The woman at the urn laughs. 'Everything's getting thinner, love. Wages, cups, patience.'
journal.ch02.ch02_crowd: Gülay: twenty-five years cleaning the plant. A contractor; she isn't on the list because she was never on the payroll.
ch02.it.ch02_crowd.l1: Familiar faces: Hasan the welder, Murat from the canteen, Gülay who cleans the floors.
ch02.it.ch02_crowd.l2: When I was little these people gave me sweets on holidays. Now every one of them holds a placard.
ch02.it.ch02_crowd.l3: Gülay touches Defne's arm. 'You're Kemal's girl? Same eyes. Stubborn.'
ch02.it.ch02_truck.l1: Riza's truck by the road. The engine is running, the wipers sweep back and forth.
ch02.it.ch02_truck.l2: Uncle Riza didn't wave. Maybe he didn't see me. Maybe he didn't want to.
ch02.it.ch02_truck.l3: When I was small he'd lift me into this cab and let me sound the horn.
journal.ch03.ch03_cabin: Riza, 34. The truck is his, bought on credit. Instalments due on the fifth of every month.
ch03.it.ch03_cabin.l1: A photo tucked behind the sun visor: two men in overalls, the factory behind them.
ch03.it.ch03_cabin.l2: Kemal and me. My first payday. He brought me over from the neighbourhood.
ch03.it.ch03_cabin.l3: Then I moved to the port; the truck paid more. It did. But nobody ever called me 'master' again.
journal.ch03.ch03_quay: The old fisherman says container 47 came before; the men unloading it wore masks.
ch03.it.ch03_quay.l1: Fishermen at the end of the quay. Fog hangs above the water.
ch03.it.ch03_quay.l2: An old fisherman speaks without reeling in. 'They brought forty-seven last week too. Wore masks unloading it.'
ch03.it.ch03_quay.l3: You wear a mask for cleaning supplies, uncle?
ch03.it.ch03_quay.l4: The fisherman doesn't answer. He casts a little further out.
ch04.it.ch04_window.l1: The factory chimney is visible from the window. No smoke for three days because of the strike.
ch04.it.ch04_window.l2: Mum used to watch that chimney to know Dad's shift was over. When the smoke stopped, he came home.
ch04.it.ch04_window.l3: There's no smoke now. Dad's home, but it's like he isn't here.
ch04.it.ch04_sofa.l1: Riza's jacket on the sofa. A fuel receipt sticks out of the pocket.
ch04.it.ch04_sofa.l2: 03:12, the port road. What was Uncle Riza hauling at three in the morning?
journal.ch04.ch04_shelf: One of the few things left from her mother: a tape labelled 'For Kemal — for the morning shift'. Her father rarely mentions her.
ch04.it.ch04_shelf.l1: On the shelf: a chipped tea glass and a cassette.
ch04.it.ch04_shelf.l2: Mum's handwriting on the tape: 'For Kemal — for the morning shift.' I never played it. I don't think Dad did either.
ch04.it.ch04_riza_talk.l1: Exam's tomorrow, right? I barely finished primary school. You finish this one, for all of us.
ch04.it.ch04_riza_talk.l2: Your ears go red when you're hiding something, Uncle Riza. Did you know?
ch04.it.ch04_riza_talk.l3: …The food's gone cold. Put another plate out for your dad.
ch06.it.ch06_board.l1: Missing-person notices and a yellowed poster: 'Workplace accidents are not fate.'
ch06.it.ch06_board.l2: Underneath, someone has added in pencil: 'If not fate, then whose?'
ch06.it.ch06_door_s.l1: Voices in the corridor. Someone says, 'Selim Aksoy's wife is here.'
ch06.it.ch06_door_s.l2: Then a baby cries. Nobody tries to hush it.
ch06.it.ch06_door.l1: Voices in the corridor: 'The factory people give statements one at a time.'
ch06.it.ch06_door.l2: Selim's voice stands out: 'I'll say what I saw. Nothing more, nothing less.'
ch07.it.ch07_window.l1: The chimney is smoking again. The robots work through the night.
ch07.it.ch07_window.l2: The smoke isn't black like before. Thinner. There are fewer people in it.
ch07.it.ch07_sofa_k.l1: Kemal's corner of the sofa is still sunken. Nobody sits there.
ch07.it.ch07_sofa_r.l1: Riza's jacket still hangs over the arm of the sofa. The fuel receipt in its pocket: 03:12.
ch07.it.ch07_sofa.l1: The sofa seats three. Tonight everyone looks set to sit at the far ends.
journal.ch07.ch07_tape: The tape is finally played. Her voice: 'Morning, Kemal. Don't forget your helmet.'
ch07.it.ch07_tape.l1: Someone finally puts the tape in the player. Hiss, then a woman's voice.
ch07.it.ch07_tape.l2: 'Morning, Kemal. Don't forget your helmet. You pick Defne up tonight.' The tape ends there.
ch08.it.ch08_tea.l1: The tea table is still there. The urn is cold, but Gülay lines up the cups anyway.
ch08.it.ch08_tea.l2: 'You set the table even if nobody comes,' she says. 'If you don't, they never will.'
journal.ch08.ch08_selim: Selim's son was born in October. His name is Umut — 'hope'.
ch08.it.ch08_selim.l1: My boy was born in October. We named him Umut. Hope. A cliché, I know.
ch08.it.ch08_selim.l2: Whatever the board says, let's walk through this gate together one more time. The rest can wait.
ch08.it.ch08_truck.l1: Riza's truck is by the road again. This time the engine is off, the cab empty.
ch08.it.ch08_truck_gone.l1: An empty parking space by the road. A truck-sized oil stain on the asphalt.
ch01.s8a_01: As he opens the locker the phone buzzes. A name saved for nine years and never called: Sevgi.
ch01.s8a_03: Kemal. It's me. Don't hang up, please. Two minutes.
ch01.s8a_04: Nine years of silence. And it fits in two minutes?
ch01.s8a_05: Defne called me. Last week. I don't know where she found my number.
ch01.s8a_06: Kemal holds the locker door. Ninth-grade Defne smiles at him from the photo.
ch01.s8a_07: She's asking about the nursing course in İzmir. About a place to stay, Kemal. She's asking me.
ch01.s8a_08: She hasn't said a word to me.
ch01.s8a_09: When could anyone ever tell you anything? When you go quiet, everybody does.
ch01.s8a_10: She was ten when you left. I waited for the school bus. I sat up with her fevers.
ch01.s8a_11: I know. And you kept my letters too, didn't you? Not one of them was ever answered.
ch01.s8a_12: A shoebox. At home, on the top shelf of the wardrobe. Nine years of letters, none of them opened.
ch01.s8a_13: You never gave them to her. Is that why she asked me, 'Why didn't you ever write?'
ch01.s8a_c1.promise: I'll give her the letters. I promise.
ch01.s8a_c1.open: My daughter goes wherever she wants.
ch01.s8a_r1: Don't promise. Do it. …Thank you, Kemal.
ch01.s8a_r2: I'm not the one interfering. Your daughter is asking. One day she'll ask you too.
ch01.s8a_r3: She needs to hear that from you, not from me. Tell her.
ch01.s8a_14: The line goes dead. The fluorescent tube hums; someone calls from behind, 'Boss, shift!'
ch01.s8b_01: A ten-minute tea break before cell three. In the maintenance corner: a hot plate, a blackened kettle and a broken stool.
ch01.s8b_02: Boss, I've got a name. Girl, Deniz. Boy, Deniz. Either way the kid looks out to sea.
ch01.s8b_03: In Karaliman the sea doesn't look back much. But it's a good name.
ch01.s8b_04: My wife said 'Let's call him Kemal', just so you know. I told her, 'The boss won't have it, he'll be embarrassed.'
ch01.s8b_04_v1: My wife said 'Let's call him Kemal.' She wanted it even more after she heard about the list. Funny. She calls you 'the man who warned us'.
ch01.s8b_05: Of course I'd be embarrassed. And he'd grow up grumpy like me, and you'd blame me.
ch01.s8b_06: The phone buzzes again. Rıza, this time.
ch01.s8b_07: Got a minute, brother? Two minutes. I won't drag it out, promise.
ch01.s8b_08: Everyone wants two minutes from me today. Go on.
ch01.s8b_09: The truck payments. Three months behind. It's not the bank, brother… It's Cevdet.
ch01.s8b_10: Cevdet from the harbour? Rıza, you don't borrow from that man. And if you do, you never finish paying; the interest never ends.
ch01.s8b_11: I know. The bank said no, the truck was sitting in the garage. What was I supposed to do?
ch01.s8b_12: Forty thousand by the end of the month. Or he takes the truck. If the truck goes, I go, brother. It's the only work I know.
ch01.s8b_13: (whispering) Is that Rıza? Tell him I've got five thousand put aside. It was for the baby, but…
ch01.s8b_c1.lend: I've got twenty thousand. We'll find the rest together.
ch01.s8b_c1.no: I don't have it either, Rıza. Defne's prep school, the rent…
ch01.s8b_c1.warn: Don't take dirty work to pay Cevdet. Whatever they offer you.
ch01.s8b_r1: Brother… I won't forget this. Next tea's on me. A thousand teas.
ch01.s8b_r2: I get it, brother. Everyone has their own fire to put out. I'll find a way.
ch01.s8b_r3: What would they offer me? …Fine, brother. Fine. I heard you.
ch01.s8b_14: The tea's gone cold. Come on, boss, to the arm. I'll watch from outside.
ch01.s8b_15: Kemal sets the glass on the counter. Cell three's yellow-and-black tape waits at the end of the corridor.
ch01.s8c_n01: The hall is empty. Kemal signs the spare sensor out of the store with his own card. His name will stay in the log; he doesn't care.
ch01.s8c_n02: Four screws, two connectors. Then calibration. It'll be done by morning.
ch01.s8c_n03: His phone buzzes three times in his pocket. All three from Defne.
ch01.s8c_n04: Dad, where are you? Dinner's cold.
ch01.s8c_n05: Dad? Uncle Rıza's here, he's waiting for you.
ch01.s8c_n06: Okay. Got it. The plant again.
ch01.s8c_nc.truth: A machine's broken, love. I stayed so nobody gets hurt.
ch01.s8c_nc.short: At work. We'll talk in the morning.
ch01.s8c_nc.none: Don't answer. Put the phone away.
ch01.s8c_nr1: The reply comes a minute later: 'Be careful. I'll wait up.' She doesn't wait up; but she doesn't delete the message either.
ch01.s8c_nr2: 'Okay.' With a full stop. Kemal knows exactly what that full stop means.
ch01.s8c_nr3: The screen goes dark. Kemal seats the sensor; for the first time in test mode, the arm stops.
ch01.s8c_n07: There. Nobody's ending up under this arm now. Not this one, at least.
ch01.s8c_n07_v1: There. This arm stops now. The letters spend one more night in the box, though. Tomorrow.
ch01.s8c_h01: Lentil soup, stale bread, football on the radio. Rıza came in saying 'I was passing by'; nobody believed him, nobody asked.
ch01.s8c_h02: Lovely soup, Defne. Your dad's cooking or yours?
ch01.s8c_h02_v1: Brother, I'll take it to Cevdet tomorrow. Thank you. For the soup, and for the rest.
ch01.s8c_h02_v2: I thought about what you said this morning, brother. Nobody's offered me anything. Yet.
ch01.s8c_h03: It's packet soup, Uncle Rıza. Let's not kid each other.
ch01.s8c_h05: The mock exam stuck at seventy-five again. Maths is eating my brain. Ece and I are going to the library on Saturday.
ch01.s8c_h06: Who's Ece? The girl with the red bike?
ch01.s8c_h07: Her bike got stolen. She walks now. Everyone walks in this town anyway.
ch01.s8c_h08: Kemal puts his spoon down. Sevgi's voice is still in his ear.
ch01.s8c_h08_v1: Kemal puts his spoon down. The shoebox sits upstairs, at the back of the shelf. He promised.
ch01.s8c_hc.hint: Are you only putting Karaliman on your list?
ch01.s8c_hc.drop: Don't ask anything. Eat your soup.
ch01.s8c_a2: She called you? Did she tell you I called her?
ch01.s8c_a3: She did. İzmir. Nursing. Why didn't you tell me?
ch01.s8c_a4: Because you'd say 'don't go'. Or you'd say nothing at all, which is worse.
ch01.s8c_a5: I'll… go have a smoke on the balcony.
ch01.s8c_a6: Rıza gets up. Two people stay in the kitchen, and nine years of silence.
ch01.s8c_a7: If you want to go, go, Defne. But the exam first.
ch01.s8c_a7_v1: There's a box upstairs. Your mother's letters. I should have given them to you. Let's open it after the exam. Together.
ch01.s8c_b1: I don't know, Dad. The list comes later. First I need the score.
ch01.s8c_b2: The score'll come. This girl's stubborn. Takes after her dad.
ch01.s8c_c1: The soup goes cold. A goal on the radio; nobody cheers.
ch01.s8c_h09: That night the only sound from Defne's room is a pencil on paper. Before bed Kemal stops at her door. He doesn't knock.
ch01.s8d_01: The lunch whistle. Kemal stands outside the canteen, a cold pide in one hand, the phone at his ear.
ch01.s8d_02: Dad? I'm out of class, I've got five minutes. You sound odd. Did something happen?
ch01.s8d_03: Nothing. My shoulder's a bit… Nothing. You tell me. How was the mock?
ch01.s8d_03_v1: My shoulder aches a bit, that's all. You tell me. How was the mock?
ch01.s8d_04: Turkish was good. Maths was a disaster again. Ece says 'if you stop panicking you'll get ten more right'. As if it's that easy.
ch01.s8d_05: Panic. At the plant we call that a sensor fault. The machine feels something, just at the wrong moment.
ch01.s8d_06: Did you prepare that metaphor as homework? Dad, are you really okay?
ch01.s8d_c1.robot: 'There's a robot. It's broken. Nobody wants to hear it.'
ch01.s8d_c1.exam: 'My only worry is your exam. Nothing else.'
ch01.s8d_r1: But you hear it. Sometimes one person hearing is enough. Mum… never mind. I was going to say something. Later.
ch01.s8d_r2: You're always tired. I think you've been tired since I was born. Okay, Dad. See you tonight.
ch01.s8d_r3: That's a lie. But a nice one. I'll take it.
ch01.s8d_07: The line goes dead. The pide has gone cold. Kemal puts it back in its bag and walks towards cell three.
ch02.s8d_01: Nevin pulls Kemal behind the guard hut. The crowd sounds muffled back here.
ch02.s8d_02: Listen, Kemal. If this gate doesn't open, the list gets longer. Not twelve, twenty. I don't write the list. They make me write it.
ch02.s8d_03: Who makes you? Demirtaş? The director's brother-in-law?
ch02.s8d_04: If I give you a name, my name goes on the list too. I've got a son as well, Kemal. At university. I pay his rent.
ch02.s8d_05: Kemal has known Nevin for fifteen years. For the first time he sees her hands shaking.
ch02.s8d_c1.selim: 'Take Selim off the list. His baby is due in October.'
ch02.s8d_c1.nothing: 'I'm not asking you for anything. Open your own gates.'
ch02.s8d_c1.prompt: What do you ask Nevin for?
ch02.s8d_r1: If one name comes off, another goes on, Kemal. Whose should I write? You tell me. …You can't, can you? Neither can I.
ch02.s8d_r2: My own gates. You're right. I've got one too; it's just that nobody keeps watch outside it.
ch02.s8d_06: Nevin drops the key into Kemal's palm and walks back to the office without looking at the crowd.
ch04.s8d_01: The balcony. Rıza has lit a cigarette and holds it without smoking. Below, a cat knocks over a bin.
ch04.s8d_02: Uncle Rıza, did you ever sit an exam?
ch04.s8d_03: My driving test. Three times. The third time the examiner took pity. 'This man was born in a truck anyway,' he said.
ch04.s8d_04: That truck belongs to Cevdet now. Half of it. The tyres, the wheel… Don't tell anyone. Not even your dad.
ch04.s8d_04_v1: You saw the envelope in my coat, didn't you? It went on Cevdet's interest. Half of it. Half the truck is still his.
ch04.s8d_06: A lot. About a year of prep school fees. Maybe two.
ch04.s8d_c1.give: 'I've got some money put away. Saved from my grant. Take it.'
ch04.s8d_c1.dad: 'You should tell Dad. He'll find a way.'
ch04.s8d_c1.quiet: Say nothing. Stand next to him.
ch04.s8d_c1.prompt: What do you tell Uncle Rıza?
ch04.s8d_r1: Take your money? Have you lost your mind? …But you offered. That's enough for me. I swear it's enough.
ch04.s8d_r2: Your dad's road always goes through a gate. Mine goes through the port. But you're right. One day I'll tell him.
ch04.s8d_r3: Defne stands next to Rıza. The cigarette burns down on its own; Rıza never takes a single drag.
ch04.s8d_07: Go on, inside. You've got an exam tomorrow, or you won't. Either way, don't catch cold.
ch02.s8a_01: Someone waves from the crowd: Ece. A bag of simit in one hand, a practice book in the other.
ch02.s8a_02: I skipped prep school. If Mr Hüsnü takes the register I'll say 'we're on strike with Defne'. Done.
ch02.s8a_03: Why did you come? Your dad doesn't work here any more.
ch02.s8a_04: That's exactly why. They let fourteen go last year and there weren't even two people at the gate. Dad didn't leave the house for three months.
ch02.s8a_05: Is the simit at least warm?
ch02.s8a_06: From this morning. Strike simit. Built to last.
ch02.s8a_07: They eat in silence for a while. Then Ece closes the book and talks without looking at the cover.
ch02.s8a_08: Defne, I don't think I'm sitting the exam. There's a job at a call centre, night shift. Mum says 'take it'.
ch02.s8a_09: I can't afford another year of studying. At least your dad has a job.
ch02.s8a_c1.study: Don't quit. We'll study at night, I'll teach you maths.
ch02.s8a_c1.free: It's your call. Whatever you choose, I'm with you.
ch02.s8a_c1.strike: The exam can wait, the job can wait. This gate first.
ch02.s8a_r1: You'll teach me maths? Aren't you the one stuck at seventy-five? …Fine. Deal.
ch02.s8a_r2: Everyone says that, then everyone goes home. But thanks. Really.
ch02.s8a_r3: Easy to say. The gate won't give you a job, Defne. But… I'm here today. Fine.
ch02.s8a_10: A voice on the loudspeaker reads out Defne's name. The committee is waiting for her.
journal.ch02.ch02_s8_board: Forty-first on the mock rankings. Last month I was fifty-third. Ece is thirty-ninth; I'm two places behind her.
ch02.it.ch02_s8_board.l1: The mock rankings on the wall. Sixty names, sixty scores. Someone has pencilled an arrow next to the forty-first name: up.
ch02.it.ch02_s8_board.l2: Forty-one. Last month, fifty-three. The arrow points up. Whoever drew it, thank you.
ch02.it.ch02_s8_window.l1: Through the window you can see the plant's chimney. No smoke today. At its foot, ant-sized, the crowd at the gate.
ch02.it.ch02_s8_window.l2: From down there it looked like a crowd. From up here it's a handful of people. Which one's true?
ch02.it.ch02_s8_desk.l1: Scratched into the edge of the desk with a compass: 'D + E, 2nd term, we'll both get in.' Someone else has added underneath: 'God willing.'
ch02.s8b_dx.objective: Look around the classroom. Mr Hüsnü is waiting at the front.
ch02.s8b_d01: Defne, sit down. The mock results are in. Maths: fourteen right. Last month, eleven.
ch02.s8b_d02: At this pace it'll be seventeen in a month. Seventeen means nursing. İzmir, Karaliman, either.
ch02.s8b_d03: Sir, there's a strike at the plant today. My dad's at the gate.
ch02.s8b_d04: I know. I stood at that gate thirty years ago. Then I became a teacher, and the gate stayed where it was.
ch02.s8b_d05: The gate matters, so do the books. But nobody reads the books for you. At the gate there are two hundred people.
ch02.s8b_d06: Ece's seat in the back row is empty. A folded note on her desk: 'Call centre, interview, 15:00.'
ch02.s8b_d06_v1: Ece is in the back row with Defne's notebook from last year. She winks.
ch02.s8b_d07: All lesson long Defne watches the plant's chimney through the window. No smoke. The strike is holding.
ch02.s8b_p00: Evening. Wood burns in an oil drum. The crowd at the gate has shrunk: twenty people, a kettle, and Selim.
ch02.s8b_p01: Zeynep called. 'Come home,' she says. 'The baby's kicking, what are you doing at a gate?'
ch02.s8b_p03: I said, 'I'm here so the baby's dad doesn't end up jobless.' She went quiet. Then she said, 'At least wrap up warm.'
ch02.s8b_p04: You were good up there, you know? You were shaking, but you were good.
ch02.s8b_p04_v1: You said let's sit at the table and half of them whistled. But the other half thought about it. That's something.
ch02.s8b_p05: Defne's phone buzzes. An unsaved İzmir number. But Defne knows it by heart.
ch02.s8b_p06: I saw the strike on the news. I thought I saw you in the crowd. Are you all right, love?
ch02.s8b_pc.warm: I'm fine, Mum. Dad's fine. Just cold.
ch02.s8b_pc.hard: Nine years, and you find me on the news?
ch02.s8b_pc.none: Don't answer. Hold your hands to the fire.
ch02.s8b_pr1: Wrap up warm. Your dad always dresses too thin; tell him. …Or don't.
ch02.s8b_pr2: You're right. But I wrote, Defne. Every year I wrote. Ask your dad.
ch02.s8b_pr3: Three dots appear on the screen, vanish, appear again. Then nothing.
ch02.s8b_p07: Who's that? A boyfriend? I won't tell the boss, don't worry.
ch02.s8b_p09: Selim doesn't say anything. He takes the kettle, fills Defne's glass, and throws another log on the fire.
ch02.s8b_m01: The sound of a chain at the gate. The shift was changing; so was the watch.
ch02.s8c_01: A black car pulls up across from the gate. The window rolls halfway down.
ch02.s8c_02: Rıza! Come here a minute. Did the truck get in or not?
ch02.s8c_02_v1: Rıza! The truck got in, well done. So the money's coming too. Come here a minute.
ch02.s8c_02_v2: Rıza! The gate stayed shut, I hear. No delivery, so no money. Come here a minute.
ch02.s8c_03: We said end of the month. There are twelve days left.
ch02.s8c_04: Twelve days is a long time, Rıza. The tyres get older, the interest gets newer. There's a job at the port; no questions, clean money.
ch02.s8c_05: A job with no questions isn't clean, man.
ch02.s8c_06: Debt is what's dirty, Rıza. The rest is just haulage.
ch02.s8c_07: From the gate Kemal hears every word. Rıza's shoulders sink a little lower with each sentence.
ch02.s8c_07_v1: From the gate Kemal hears every word. The twenty thousand he gave hasn't covered even a week of this man's interest.
ch02.s8c_c1.face: Walk to the car: 'Rıza's debt is my debt. Talk to me.'
ch02.s8c_c1.out: Stay out of it. It's Rıza's business.
ch02.s8c_r1: Kemal! Do you owe me as well? No. Then you have nothing to say. But I won't forget your face.
ch02.s8c_r1b: Brother, you didn't have to. …But thanks.
ch02.s8c_r2: Kemal looks away. The car window rolls up; Rıza stands alone in the middle of the road for a while.
ch02.s8c_08: A port job, he said. Always the port. I don't take a load without knowing what's in it, brother. I don't… right?
ch03.it.ch03_s8_tv.l1: Strike footage on the news, sound off. The caption: 'Workers at the gate in Karaliman.' Nobody in the teahouse looks up.
ch03.it.ch03_s8_tv.l2: Kemal flashed up for a second. In his helmet. Nobody recognised him. I did.
journal.ch03.ch03_s8_counter: According to İlyas, the tea boy, half the port is in Cevdet's ledger. Nobody wants to be the last one.
ch03.it.ch03_s8_counter.l1: İlyas, the tea boy, lines up the glasses. He talks without looking at Rıza.
ch03.it.ch03_s8_counter.l2: 'Half the port's in that ledger, Rıza. You're not the first. But nobody wants to be the last.'
ch03.it.ch03_s8_backgammon.l1: Two old dockers play backgammon. One blows on the dice before every throw; he hasn't won in thirty years.
ch03.it.ch03_s8_backgammon.l2: My dad used to blow on them too. He never won either. But he always blew.
ch03.it.ch03_s8_window.l1: Behind the glass, the port lights. One crane holds a container in mid-air, as if it can't make up its mind.
ch03.s8a_x.objective: Walk around the teahouse. Cevdet is waiting at the corner table.
ch03.s8a_01: In the harbour teahouse the TV is on with the sound off. At the corner table sits Cevdet, two teas and a ledger in front of him.
ch03.s8a_02: Sit down, Rıza. Don't let your tea go cold. The interest never cools down; the tea might as well stay warm.
ch03.s8a_03: We said end of the month, Cevdet.
ch03.s8a_04: We did. So does the ledger. Forty principal, eleven interest, four late fee. Fifty-five thousand, Rıza. Not forty.
ch03.s8a_04_v1: We did. Kemal's money came in, I wrote it down. But interest grows by itself. Still thirty-five thousand, Rıza.
ch03.s8a_05: Fifty-five? I've already paid you half the truck.
ch03.s8a_06: You paid half, half is mine. The tyres are mine, the wheel is mine. You're just the driver.
ch03.s8a_07: There's a container, number forty-seven, at the port tonight. The dispatcher will hand you an envelope. Take it, haul the load. Half your interest disappears.
ch03.s8a_c1.beg: Give me one more month. One month. I'm begging like a kid.
ch03.s8a_c1.proud: I know what goes in my truck. I don't haul what I don't know.
ch03.s8a_c1.truck: Put the papers on the table: 'Take the truck. We're done.'
ch03.s8a_r1: Don't beg, Rıza, it doesn't suit you. I won't give you a month. I'll give you a night. Tonight.
ch03.s8a_r2: Of course you know. And you know how to forget what you know. Everybody does, Rıza.
ch03.s8a_r3: (He pushes the papers back.) What use is the truck parked at my place? Let it work for you. Tonight.
ch03.s8a_08: Cevdet leaves without paying for his tea. The tea boy looks at Rıza, then quietly writes it on Rıza's tab.
ch03.s8b_01: Rıza climbs into the cab and pulls the door shut. In the glovebox, his father's photo: in front of this same truck, thirty years ago, moustached and proud.
ch03.s8b_02: Did you ever haul a load you didn't know, Dad? Course you did. Everybody did. And nobody asked afterwards.
ch03.s8b_03: The radio plays a late-night show. The host reads out someone's request for a break-up song. Rıza leaves it on.
ch03.s8b_04: Kemal and I started at this port. Fifteen years old. He climbed the cranes, I counted the crates. Then he went to the plant and I took the wheel.
ch03.s8b_05: The phone buzzes. A message. Defne.
ch03.s8b_06: Uncle Rıza, are you asleep? Could you drive me to the exam that morning? Dad might be stuck on shift. I don't trust the bus.
ch03.s8b_c1.yes: 'Exam morning, eight o'clock, at your door. We'll go in the truck, everyone'll stare.'
ch03.s8b_r1: In the truck! Can Ece come? The cab's huge anyway. Thanks, Uncle Rıza, thank you so much!
ch03.s8b_07: Exam morning, eight. Let me just get this load done first.
ch03.s8c_01: Four in the morning. The port road is empty. The streetlights go out one by one, as if someone behind him is switching them off.
ch03.s8c_02_v1: A message from Cevdet: 'They say the load never arrived. We'll talk.'
ch03.s8c_02_v2: A message from Cevdet: 'You didn't bring it, but the load arrived. Interest stays.'
ch03.s8c_03: The money in the envelope goes on Cevdet's interest. The principal stays put. And container forty-seven stays with me. In here.
ch03.s8c_03_v1: I didn't take the envelope. The interest ticked on anyway. But at least that money isn't burning my hand. Forty-seven stays with me all the same. In here.
ch03.s8c_05: Rıza turns off the engine outside his place but doesn't get out. He sits in the cab until dawn.
ch03.s8c_05_v1: Rıza types a note into his phone: 'Exam morning, 08:00, Defne.' He underlines it twice.
ch03.s8c_06: Behind him the port keeps working, as if nothing had happened.
ch04.s8a_01: The doorbell. Ece on the step, wet hair and a bag of tangerines.
ch04.s8a_02: Last night. Last revision. Let's write out the formulas once more, then I swear I'll go.
ch04.s8a_02_v1: I went to the interview. They took me. Night shift, I start Monday. I'm not sitting the exam, Defne. I came to tell you.
ch04.s8a_02_v2: Three nights on the picket. Mum's going to throw me out. But I'm sitting the exam, because of you. Write out the formulas.
ch04.s8a_03: Uncle Rıza's in the living room, Dad's in the kitchen. Nobody's talking. Perfect study conditions.
ch04.s8a_04: Nobody talks at my place either. The difference is our TV shouts.
ch04.s8a_05: They sit at the table. Derivatives, integrals on the paper, and a tiny heart in the corner. Ece scribbles it out; Defne draws it again.
ch04.s8a_06: If one of us gets in, she takes the other along. Deal? İzmir, Ankara, wherever.
ch04.s8a_06_v1: If you get in, don't forget me. I'll look at your photos on the night shift.
ch04.s8a_08: When Ece leaves, the tangerines stay on the table. Their peel warms on the radiator; the house feels a little more like a home.
ch04.s8b_k01: Defne, a minute. Before we talk… I need to give you this.
ch04.s8b_k02: Kemal takes a shoebox down from the top shelf. He wipes the dust with his hand; it isn't enough.
ch04.s8b_k03: Your mother's letters. Nine years. I never opened one. I never gave them to you. I don't even know why. I was scared, I suppose.
ch04.s8b_f01: Looking for a blanket in the bedroom, Defne reaches for the top shelf. A shoebox falls; the lid comes off.
ch04.s8b_f02: Envelopes. Dozens. All sealed. All in the same handwriting: 'To Defne.' Postmarks: İzmir.
ch04.s8b_f03: She wrote. Every year she wrote. And Dad… kept them.
ch04.s8b_f03_v1: 'I wrote, ask your dad,' she said. And I said she'd found me on the news after nine years. She wrote. Dad kept them.
ch04.s8b_r1: (letter) 'My Defne, today you turned eleven. I couldn't make your cake. I lit a candle in the kitchen and blew it out for you. I won't tell you my wish; then it won't come true.'
ch04.s8b_r1b: When I was eleven. That day Dad brought a cake home from the plant. The icing was squashed. I cried, and not about the icing.
ch04.s8b_r2: The lid goes back on. But Defne doesn't put the box back on the shelf; she puts it under her own desk.
ch04.s8b_r3: Because I didn't want you losing a mother all over again every year. …No. Because I didn't want to lose. Not you too.
ch04.s8b_end: In the living room Rıza turns the TV down. Everyone is waiting for the next thing to be said.
ch04.s8c_g01: Defne puts on her coat. She lays the entry slip and her ID in the middle of the desk and sets an eraser on top so they won't blow away.
ch04.s8c_g02: Maybe I'll make it. Half past nine. Straight from the plant to the school in the morning. It could work. Could it?
ch04.s8c_g03: (text) Where are you going at this hour?! Defne. DEFNE. Nine thirty tomorrow!
ch04.s8c_g03_v1: (text) I'm on nights now too. We're both awake. Be careful, okay?
ch04.s8c_g04: The door closes quietly behind her. On the desk, seventeen-year-old Defne waits on her ID card.
ch04.s8c_01: Midnight. In Defne's room: a desk lamp, a pencil pot, her ID card, two pencils and an eraser.
ch04.s8c_02: ID, entry slip, pencils. Three things. A whole year fits into three things.
ch04.s8c_03: Rıza's message sits on her phone screen.
ch04.s8c_03_v1: Rıza's note on her screen: 'Exam morning, eight. Truck's ready. I won't honk, promise.'
ch04.s8c_04: (text) Can't sleep. You? By the way I forgot pi. Joking. 3.14. Go to bed.
ch04.s8c_04_v1: (text) Good luck. I'm thinking about my first night shift. Write for me as well, okay?
ch04.s8c_06: One envelope from the box lies at the edge of the desk; opened, read, folded again.
ch04.s8c_06_v1: The box under the desk stays shut. But Defne sits with her foot resting against it; she wants to know it's there.
ch04.s8c_07: In the kitchen her father brews tea. Nobody will drink it; it's so the house knows someone is awake.
ch05.s8a_01: A thermos, a cheese sandwich, work gloves. Kemal gets ready for the night shift. Rıza has dozed off on the sofa; the TV talks to itself.
ch05.s8a_02: Defne has fallen asleep at her desk, a pencil mark on her cheek.
ch05.s8a_02_v1: Defne has her coat on and is waiting at the door: 'I'll carry the thermos.'
ch05.s8a_02_v2: The light in Defne's room goes out. Then on again. Then out again.
ch05.s8a_02_v3: Defne's coat is gone from the hook. A note on the table: 'On the picket. Don't be cross.'
ch05.s8a_03: Rıza. Up. Go home; at least sleep on your own sofa.
ch05.s8a_04: I wasn't asleep, brother. I was thinking. I think with my eyes shut, it works better.
ch05.s8a_05: Cevdet called. There's another job tonight, behind the plant. I'm not going. But I'll go and tell him I'm not going.
ch05.s8a_05_v1: Brother… I need to tell you about that envelope. But not tonight. Tonight Cevdet called; there's another job, behind the plant.
ch05.s8a_07: I don't know, brother. There's a lot I don't know lately.
ch05.s8a_07_v1: Whatever they offer, you said. They keep offering, brother. They never stop.
ch05.s8a_08: Rıza leaves. A message on Kemal's phone. Sevgi.
ch05.s8a_09: Her exam's coming. Wish her luck from me. Or don't; up to you.
ch05.s8a_09_v1: I'm not interfering. I just know her exam is close. That's all.
ch05.s8a_c1.bridge: 'Write to her yourself. You have her number. I won't mind.'
ch05.s8a_r1: Sent. A minute later, a one-word reply: 'Thanks.' The longest conversation they've had in nine years.
ch05.s8a_r2: Kemal types it, deletes it, types it again. 'I will.' Then he looks at Defne's door.
ch05.s8a_r3: The phone goes in his pocket. The message stays marked as read; Sevgi will see that.
ch05.s8b_01: In the A&E corridor: wet coats, the smell of soot and a broken tea machine.
ch05.s8b_02: Selim's arm is bandaged. Zeynep sits beside him, one hand holding his, the other on her belly.
ch05.s8b_02_v1: Zeynep sits at the end of the corridor, both hands on her belly. Nobody dares go near her.
ch05.s8b_03: Did everyone get out? Somebody tell me. Did everyone get out?
ch05.s8b_03_v1: The boss pushed me all the way to the door. Then… why didn't he come out? Somebody tell me.
ch05.s8b_04: The truck's headlights must still be on. I didn't switch them off. Nobody will now.
ch05.s8b_04_v1: I took down the wall. Twenty-two people came out through that hole. I counted. I couldn't stop counting.
ch05.s8b_04_v2: I left. I pulled the truck back and I left. Nobody look at me. Please.
ch05.s8b_05: Has anyone seen Defne? …All right. All right. I see her.
ch05.s8b_05_v1: The exam's at half nine. Nobody tell her anything. Let her finish first.
ch05.s8b_06: Kemal sits down on a chair and doesn't get up. He's holding Defne's thermos, opening and closing the lid.
ch05.s8b_07: Dad's hands are black. Someone give him water. Please, someone give him some water.
ch05.s8b_07_v1: They brought a helmet. Dad's helmet. Why are they bringing me a helmet?
ch05.s8b_08: Eight o'clock. The exam. I promised.
ch05.s8b_09: Rıza climbs into the truck with soot on his face and picks Defne up at her door. Neither speaks on the way. At the school gate Defne takes out her ID and goes in without looking back.
ch05.s8b_09_v1: The truck is still stuck in the wall. Rıza flags down a taxi and picks Defne up at her door. At the school gate she takes out her ID and goes in without looking back.
ch05.s8b_10: In Room 4 Defne opens the exam booklet. Her phone is off. She reads the first question; reads it; reads it again.
ch05.s8b_11: (text) I saw the news. Defne, call me. Please. Just write 'I'm okay'.
ch05.s8b_12: By eight o'clock nobody in the corridor is talking. The tea machine beeps once, then it too falls silent.
ch05.s8b_12_v1: Nobody in the corridor is waiting for them. The tea machine beeps once, then it too falls silent.
ch05.it.ch05_s8_machine.l1: A sign on the machine says 'OUT OF ORDER'. Someone has added underneath: 'Aren't we all.' Three coins sit beside it; nobody has taken them.
journal.ch05.ch05_s8_window: From the hospital window you could see the smoke from the plant. Morning came, but the smoke didn't go.
ch05.it.ch05_s8_window.l1: Through the window, a grey band over the town. Smoke from the plant. The wind isn't carrying it out to sea, but over the houses.
ch05.it.ch05_s8_zeynep.l1: The doctor said 'the baby's fine'. The baby's fine. I keep telling everyone, so I'll believe it myself.
ch05.it.ch05_s8_desk.l1: The duty nurse reads out the list: the injured, their ages, their rooms. She doesn't lower her voice; she has no strength left to.
ch05.s8b_x.objective: Wait in the corridor. Go to the nurses' desk when you're ready.
ch05.s8d_01: Room 4. The desks are the same as at the prep school, the board the same. One of the invigilators is familiar: Mr Hüsnü.
ch05.s8d_02: Phones off, into the envelopes. Pencils on the desk. Nobody looks at anybody; and if you do, I didn't see it.
ch05.s8d_03: Defne's phone buzzes once inside the envelope. Then again. Then without stopping.
ch05.s8d_04: I switched it off. I did switch it off, didn't I?
ch05.s8d_05: Defne. The phone is in the envelope. You are here. This first.
ch05.s8d_06: (from the back row, whispering) Breathe. Pi is three point one four. The rest will come.
ch05.s8d_07: The first question is a passage: 'The industrialisation of a town…' Defne reads it three times. On the fourth, the words fall into place.
ch05.s8d_08: 12:45. Defne leaves the last question blank, puts down her pencil and opens the envelope.
ch06.s8d_01: Let's start from the top. Three weeks ago, the welding robot in cell three. Its sensor was dead.
ch06.s8d_01_v1: Let's start from the top. The robot in cell three. Somebody replaced its sensor at night. The name's in the log: Kemal Arslan.
ch06.s8d_01_v2: Let's start from the top. The robot in cell three. Somebody wrote a report. It was found in a drawer; nobody had read it.
ch06.s8d_01_v3: Let's start from the top. The robot in cell three. Somebody signed it off as 'OK'. The sensor was dead.
ch06.s8d_02: Then the strike. The gate stayed shut, but the barrels got in anyway. How?
ch06.s8d_02_v1: Then the strike. The gate opened, a truck went in. What was that truck carrying?
ch06.s8d_03: Container forty-seven. 'Cleaning supplies', according to the port records.
ch06.s8d_03_v1: Container forty-seven. I have a photo. I know who took it and who it was sent to.
ch06.s8d_03_v2: Container forty-seven. The barrels turned up in the old fish depot. Who knows about that depot?
ch06.s8d_04: I hauled it. Without knowing what it was. …No. Knowing. Choosing not to know.
ch06.s8d_05: I kept a photo hidden. And a box of letters. I opened both too late.
ch06.s8d_06: I knew about that arm. Everybody did. Knowing wasn't enough.
ch06.s8d_07: Everyone knows a piece. Nobody knows the whole. Or somebody does, and they're sitting across from me, saying nothing.
loc.ch07.s8_port: The port · The night before the last shift
ch07.s8d_01: Midnight. The port works the way it always does. Cranes, trucks, loads nobody asks about.
ch07.s8d_02: Dad and Uncle Rıza started at this port when they were fifteen. I'm nineteen. Four years late for something; I don't know what.
ch07.s8d_03: Thirty years ago I used to climb those cranes. From up there the town looked small. Now it looks small from down here as well.
ch07.s8d_04: Forty-seven is gone. Another forty-seven has taken its place. There's always a forty-seven.
ch07.s8d_05: A message: 'We'll be at the gate at six tomorrow. Come too.' From: Ece.
ch07.s8d_05_v1: A photo arrives from Defne's phone: Ece, Mr Hüsnü and a thermos. Underneath: 'Six tomorrow.'
ch07.s8d_06: One of the cranes sets a container down. The sound travels to the far end of the port and does not come back.
ch08.s8d_01: The board wants a name. From me. Twenty years I've been writing names; for the first time I'm thinking of writing my own.
ch08.s8d_01_v1: Demirtaş is in the papers. The board still wants a name; a worker's name. Twenty years I've written names. Today I won't.
ch08.s8d_02: The crowd falls silent. The fog drips, drop by drop, from the bars of the gate.
ch06.s8a_01: Five-minute break. I've ordered tea. Don't run off, the door's locked anyway.
ch06.s8a_r01: The phone buzzes on the table. One word on the screen: Cevdet.
ch06.s8a_r02: Rıza, my lion. They say you're at the station. So what are you going to tell them? The barrels, the envelope, the interest?
ch06.s8a_r03: I've got the truck's papers, you know that. One wrong word and the tow truck is at your door tomorrow morning.
ch06.s8a_r04: Cevdet, people burned last night. And you're still talking interest?
ch06.s8a_r05: I talk interest, Rıza. Plenty of people talk about fires.
ch06.s8a_rc.tell: I'll tell them about Cevdet too. The ledger, the interest, all of it.
ch06.s8a_rc.hang: Hang up. Only answer what they ask.
ch06.s8a_rc.prompt: How much will you tell the commissioner?
ch06.s8a_rr1: Write this down, Cevdet: Rıza Yıldız. In debt. But not afraid any more.
ch06.s8a_rr2: Rıza turns the phone face down. Its light keeps blinking against the table.
ch06.s8a_d01: Three messages on Defne's phone. One from Ece, one from Mr Hüsnü, one from an unsaved İzmir number.
ch06.s8a_d02: (text) Where are you? They said you're at the station. Mum says 'stay away from that girl'. I'm at the door.
ch06.s8a_d02_v1: (text) Came straight from my shift. I'm at the door. I haven't slept and I know you haven't either.
ch06.s8a_d03: (text) Defne, whatever you've been through, you've been through it. The exam comes round again. You only come round once. Look after yourself.
ch06.s8a_d04: (text) I'm outside the station. Came on the night bus. If you don't want to see me, I'll go. I'm just here.
ch06.s8a_d05: Nine years. One night bus. Nine years fit into one night bus.
ch06.s8a_k01: Kemal's phone rings. Unknown number. He answers.
ch06.s8a_k02: Kemal, it's Zeynep. Selim's… Selim's asleep. He asked me to thank you. He can't say it himself, he keeps crying.
ch06.s8a_k02_v1: Kemal, it's Zeynep. I won't ask you anything. Just… were you the last to hear his voice that night? What did he say?
ch06.s8a_k03: Zeynep… Have you named the baby?
ch06.s8a_k03_v1: 'Boss,' he said. Just 'boss'. Then the smoke.
ch06.s8a_k04: Deniz. Girl or boy. That's what Selim wanted.
ch06.s8a_end: The door opens. The tea arrives; so does the commissioner. The five minutes are over.
ch06.it.ch06_s8_press.l1: Two reporters, one camera. One of them is on the phone to the newsroom: 'No names. Everyone's keeping quiet.'
ch06.it.ch06_s8_bench.l1: A glove someone left on the bench. Plant issue, the palm scorched. Anyone could guess whose it is; nobody picks it up.
journal.ch06.ch06_s8_poster: A lost-dog poster outside the station: 'Brown dog, lost on the night of the strike. Answers to Paşa.' Three phone numbers below.
ch06.it.ch06_s8_poster.l1: 'Lost: brown dog, answers to Paşa. Went missing the night of the strike.' Three phone numbers below, in three different hands.
ch06.s8b_x.objective: Stand at the top of the steps. Walk down when you're ready.
ch06.s8b_r01: The black car is there again. This time the window comes all the way down.
ch06.s8b_r02: I don't know what you told them, Rıza. But the commissioner looked at me twice today. I didn't like it.
ch06.s8b_r02_v1: They asked for my ledger, Rıza. My ledger. In thirty years nobody's ever asked for that ledger.
ch06.s8b_r03: Hand over the keys. We close the account. The truck's mine, you're free.
ch06.s8b_rc.give: Toss the keys in through the window.
ch06.s8b_rc.keep: 'The truck stays with me. We'll talk about the debt in court.'
ch06.s8b_rr1: The keys land in Cevdet's lap. Rıza lets go of thirty years behind the wheel in a second and walks away. He feels light. The lightness scares him.
ch06.s8b_rr2: Court? You? …We'll see, Rıza. We'll see.
ch06.s8b_rr3: The car pulls away. Rıza squeezes the key in his fist until its teeth dig into his palm.
ch06.s8b_d01: A woman at the bottom of the steps. Around forty, in a thin coat. A crumpled bus ticket in her hand.
ch06.s8b_d02: You're shorter than in the photos.
ch06.s8b_d03: And you're tall. Like your dad. …I'm sorry. I rehearsed what to say and I've forgotten all of it.
ch06.s8b_d03_v1: If you're wondering about the wish on your eleventh-birthday candle… I wished 'that one day she opens the door'. Have you? I don't know yet.
ch06.s8b_d04_v1: I heard about your dad. Could I… come to the funeral? If you'll let me.
ch06.s8b_dc.hug: Walk down the steps. Hold her.
ch06.s8b_dc.pass: Walk past her. Ece is waiting for you.
ch06.s8b_dr1: At first Sevgi doesn't know what to do; she's forgotten how to open her arms. Then she remembers. Nobody speaks. Ece watches from a distance and wipes her eyes.
ch06.s8b_dr2: Tea. Fine. Tea's good. You took it without sugar, didn't you? …No. I don't know. Tell me.
ch06.s8b_dr3: Defne walks down the steps and past Sevgi. No voice calls after her. She takes Ece's arm; at the corner she looks back, once.
ch06.s8b_k01: Sevgi is standing at the bottom of the steps. After nine years. She has come for the funeral.
ch06.s8b_kc.give: Fetch the box and give it to her: 'These were hers. Now they're yours.'
ch06.s8b_kc.prompt: The shoebox is in the car
ch06.s8b_kr1: Sevgi doesn't open the box. She presses it to her chest and stands like that. For the first time Kemal notices how heavy it was.
ch06.s8b_kr2: They stand side by side. A bus goes past, then another. Neither of them gets on.
ch07.it.ch07_s8_sea.l1: At the foot of the slope the sea, grey and calm. The cranes are working at the port. From up here they look like toys.
journal.ch07.ch07_s8_bench: Someone left a thermos on the cemetery bench. There was still warm tea in it.
ch07.it.ch07_s8_bench.l1: A thermos on the bench. Steam rises when you open it; the tea is still warm. Whoever left it wanted someone to sit down.
ch07.s8a_cx.objective: Walk through the cemetery. Go to the new stones when you're ready.
ch07.s8a_m01: The cemetery sits on a slope facing the sea. The wind never drops; everyone who brings flowers weighs them down with stones.
ch07.s8a_m02: A new stone: 'Kemal Arslan. Maintenance foreman.' In front of it, a pair of work gloves someone left.
ch07.s8a_m03: A new stone: 'Defne Arslan.' In front of it, an exam entry slip wrapped in plastic; nobody has had the heart to take it.
ch07.s8a_m04: A new stone: 'Rıza Yıldız. Driver.' On top, a truck key ring; a rubber duck, half melted.
ch07.s8a_m05: A new stone: 'Selim Aksoy.' In front of it, under a pebble, an ultrasound photo.
ch07.s8a_m06: Deniz is asleep. Born in October, just like he said. I play her a recording of her father's voice; he's laughing in that one too.
ch07.s8a_m07: I said I'd come every Sunday. I came the first Sunday. The second it rained; I came anyway. I don't know about the third.
ch07.s8a_m08: I don't come here to talk. I just wipe the dust off the stone. With my hand. As if I were fixing something.
ch07.s8a_m09: I come in the truck and wait at the gate. Thirty years weren't enough to walk in. I need another thirty.
ch07.s8a_m10: I know I don't belong here. But I don't know where else I belong any more.
ch07.s8a_m11: The wind knocks a stone over and a flower flies off. Someone runs after it, puts it back and weighs it down with two stones this time.
ch07.s8a_s01: The doorbell. Selim, with a blanket in his arms; inside the blanket, Deniz. Behind him Zeynep, holding a tray of baklava.
ch07.s8a_s02: Born in October. Just like I promised. Three kilos two hundred. Here, boss, hold her. Don't be scared, she doesn't bite.
ch07.s8a_s03: I… the last one I held like this was Defne. Nineteen years ago. My hands have forgotten.
ch07.s8a_s04: Hands don't forget, Kemal. You think you've forgotten, and meanwhile your hands are already holding.
ch07.s8a_s05: Deniz, I'm your uncle Rıza. I'm going to teach you to drive a truck. Don't tell your dad.
ch07.s8a_s06: And I'll teach you maths. How not to get stuck at seventy-five.
ch07.s8a_s07: The baby cries, then stops, then grabs Kemal's finger and won't let go. That evening, for the first time, everyone in the house laughs at once.
ch07.s8b_01: From outside, the beeping of a tow truck reversing. Beep. Beep. Beep.
ch07.s8b_02: Cevdet. So he's come. Didn't wait for court.
ch07.s8b_02_v1: Cevdet. Came even with his ledger at the police station. To take one last thing.
ch07.s8b_03.stand: Stand in front of the tow truck.
ch07.s8b_03.let: Let him take it. No more fighting over a truck.
ch07.s8b_03.prompt: The tow truck is at the door
ch07.s8b_r1: The tow truck stops. Neighbours come to their windows; one opens a door, then another. Cevdet's driver switches off the engine, lights a cigarette and walks away.
ch07.s8b_r2: The truck is hooked up and disappears at the end of the street. Rıza waves after it; at whom, he doesn't know.
ch07.s8b_04: A message on Defne's phone: 'Placement results have been announced.'
ch07.s8b_i1: Go. Take a thermos. They have night shifts there too. Nurses do.
ch07.s8b_i1_v1: Defne hears her own voice and is surprised. What would Dad say? 'Take a thermos.' She laughs.
ch07.s8b_i2: Defne deletes the message. Then restores it from the bin. Then turns the phone face down. The decision could wait one more night.
ch08.s8a_01: Six in the morning. Fog clings to the bars of the gate. Not many people, but familiar faces.
ch08.s8a_02: Mr Hüsnü has come with a thermos of tea. 'It was a morning like this thirty years ago,' he says, to nobody in particular.
ch08.s8a_03: Came straight from my shift. Headset still round my neck. 'Customer satisfaction', they call it. Nobody asks about mine.
ch08.s8a_03_v1: My result came: Karaliman Vocational School, lab technician. Not bad. Thanks to your maths. I'm here.
ch08.s8a_03_v2: I learnt everything on that picket. Including how to stand at a gate. I'm here.
ch08.s8a_04: I brought Deniz. So that when she's grown she can say: 'I was there too.'
ch08.s8a_05: Boss, I took the robot apart last week. It's going to another city. While I was removing the arm I stopped for a second. The sensor… the sensor worked.
ch08.s8a_05_v1: Boss, I took the robot apart last week. Your handwriting was on the sensor: 'Replaced — K.' I cried. Don't tell anyone.
ch08.s8a_06: A horn from the end of the road. Two short blasts. The truck; everyone knows that sound.
ch08.s8a_07: Cevdet's tow truck came and went. The truck's mine. The papers are with the court, the wheel's with me. This morning the engine ran just to get me here.
ch08.s8a_08: I came by bus. First time I've come to this gate as a passenger. Strange.
ch08.s8a_09: At the edge of the crowd stands a woman in a thin coat. Sevgi. Not coming any closer, but not leaving either.
ch08.s8a_10: Mum came. Dad's at the gate. Ece with her headset, Mr Hüsnü with his thermos. If someone had told me this would happen, I wouldn't have believed it.
ch08.s8a_10_v1: The ticket's in my pocket. İzmir, the nine o'clock evening bus. But this morning first. This gate first.
ch08.s8a_11: Nevin walks to the gate with the board members. Nobody puts down their tea.
ch08.s8b_01: As the crowd breaks up, Deniz starts to cry. Zeynep rocks her; Mr Hüsnü shares out the last of the tea so nobody's glass is empty.
ch08.s8b_02: Next time there'll be more of us at the gate. That's how it always starts: twenty people first.
ch08.s8b_03: Sevgi makes her way through the crowd, straightens Defne's collar and steps back without a word.
ch08.s8b_04: The fog lifts. One letter is missing from the sign above the gate; nobody remembers how long it's been missing.
ch03.s8e_01: While the envelope still hangs in the dispatcher's window, Rıza's phone rings. On the screen: 'Mum.'
ch03.s8e_01_v1: With the envelope in his inside pocket, Rıza's phone rings. On the screen: 'Mum.'
ch03.s8e_02: Son, aren't you asleep? I couldn't sleep. I dreamt of the truck; it had no wheels.
ch03.s8e_03: It's a dream, Mum. The wheels are fine. Four of them, plus the spare.
ch03.s8e_04: I sold my bracelets for that truck, remember. The bracelets your father gave me. As long as the truck's all right and you're all right, I don't mourn the gold.
ch03.s8e_05: That man Cevdet came to the door the other day. 'Say hello to Rıza,' he said. I didn't like the hello, son.
ch03.s8e_c1.truth: 'Mum, I owe Cevdet. Half the truck is his. But I'll sort it out.'
ch03.s8e_c1.lie: 'Just an old customer, Mum. A hello's a hello. Go to sleep.'
ch03.s8e_c1.prompt: What do you tell your mother?
ch03.s8e_r1: I knew it. You can't fool your mother; I gave birth to you. Sort it out. But sort it out clean, Rıza. Don't let dirt into your father's truck.
ch03.s8e_r2: All right, son. I'll sleep. You sleep too. …Rıza? You always say 'Mum' when you're lying. Just so you know.
ch03.s8e_06: Dad's truck. Don't let dirt in. Easy to say, Mum.
ch05.s8e_01: Rıza is on the port road. Cevdet's man has just called: 'Wait at the plant's back ramp. You'll pick something up and leave something behind.'
ch05.s8e_02: Pick something up, leave something behind. Leave what? My conscience?
ch05.s8e_03: As he rounds the bend, the sky is orange. Smoke rises from the roof of the plant.
ch05.s8e_04: Kemal's inside. Defne… Defne might be inside too. God. God, just once. Let me make it just once.
ch05.s8e_04_v1: Kemal's inside. Defne's at her exam, thank God. God, just once. Let me make it just once.
ch07.s8e_01: One extra plate in the kitchen. Sevgi has missed the İzmir bus twice; she made sure to be late for the third.
ch07.s8e_02: Where's the salt? Nine years ago it was in that cupboard.
ch07.s8e_03: Still there. Dad never moves anything. He just put a box on the top shelf once.
ch07.s8e_05: When you sat down at this table there was always one empty chair. Mine, I know. Today it's taken. I don't know if that's enough.
ch07.s8e_05_v1: There was always one empty chair at this table; mine. Now a different chair is empty. I won't sit in it. I promise.
ch07.s8e_06: Sevgi, I'd forgotten the taste of this soup. It's lentil, isn't it? Kemal's was always out of a packet.
ch07.s8e_c1.leave: 'Don't miss the bus. See you at the gate tomorrow.'
ch07.s8e_c1.prompt: Sevgi gets up; time for the bus
ch07.s8e_r1: Sevgi sleeps on the sofa with her coat over her. At two in the morning Defne gets up and puts a blanket over her, the way Sevgi used to do for her nine years ago.
ch07.s8e_r2: Sevgi stops at the door as if to say something, then doesn't. Footsteps on the stairs, then a bus engine.
ch08.s8e_01: Thirty years ago we stood at this gate for fourteen days. On the fifteenth the gate opened, we went in and got our jobs back. A year later they sold the plant.
ch08.s8e_02: Did we win? Did we lose? I don't know. But I still remember those fourteen days. Not the plant; I remember the gate.
ch08.s8e_03: Sir, why didn't you ever tell us this in class?
ch08.s8e_05: For the first time, someone at the gate laughs. Then someone else. Even Nevin.
loc.ch08.s8_home: Home · The morning of the last shift · 05:10
ch08.s8f_01: Ten past five. The ironing board is up in the kitchen. Nobody is ironing; but nobody folds it away either.
ch08.s8f_02: Do overalls need ironing? Twenty years I never ironed them. Today I will.
ch08.s8f_03: The ticket's in my bag. The nine o'clock bus tonight. But the gate first. Gate first, then İzmir. That's the order.
ch08.s8f_04: I didn't sleep. But this time not because I'm scared. Excitement, I think. When did I last feel that?
ch08.s8f_05: Sevgi is asleep on the sofa, still in her coat. The blanket has slipped to the floor.
ch08.s8f_06: (on the phone) I'm downstairs. I won't honk; let the neighbours sleep. But I'm downstairs.
ch08.s8f_07: The kettle whistles. The glasses are set out; one too many. Nobody puts it back.
ch08.s8f_07_v1: The kettle whistles. The glasses are set out. Habit: one too many. Nobody puts it back; that glass would stay on the table today as well.
ch08.s8f_c1.dinner: 'I'll be back for dinner. Lentil soup.'
ch08.s8f_c1.none: Leave no note. Close the door quietly.
ch08.s8f_c1.prompt: Leave a note on the table before you go
ch08.s8f_r1: The note goes under the kettle. The word 'lentil' is underlined twice.
ch08.s8f_r2: The note stays in the middle of the table. The word 'fine' is written a little shakily; the writer didn't notice, or didn't want to.
ch08.s8f_r3: The door closes quietly. The lock turns once. The flat is so quiet it might think nobody had left.
ch08.s8f_08: The stairs, the street, the fog. Twenty minutes to the gate. The same road for twenty years.
ch08.it.ch08_s8_hoca.l1: Tea? No glasses, but the thermos lid will do. Thirty years ago we drank out of thermos lids as well.
ch08.it.ch08_s8_hoca.l2: I always tell my students: 'read the passage twice'. Life's the same. This is my second reading of this gate.
journal.ch08.ch08_s8_ece: Ece came to the gate straight from her shift. She still had her headset on: 'if I take it off, I'll fall asleep.'
ch08.it.ch08_s8_ece.l1: I spoke to a hundred and twelve people tonight. All angry, all right, and I couldn't do a thing for any of them. Here at least I'm on my feet.
ch08.it.ch08_s8_ece.l2: Tell Defne… or don't. I'll tell her. Our deal still stands.
ch08.it.ch08_s8_zeynep.l1: It's Deniz's first fog. Her eyes are wide open, as if she's looking for something.
ch08.it.ch08_s8_zeynep.l2: Selim said 'don't take her out in the cold'. And I said 'she should know this cold'. I suppose we're both right.
ch08.it.ch08_s8_zeynep_s.l1: It's Deniz's first fog. Selim loved fog. 'The plant's hiding,' he used to say. 'Shall we skip work today?'
ch08.it.ch08_s8_zeynep_s.l2: Today we're not going to work. Today we came to the gate. In his place.
ch08.it.ch08_s8_sevgi.l1: I don't know what I'm doing here. I left this gate behind me nine years ago. I suppose coming back is a road too.
ch08.it.ch08_s8_sevgi.l2: In the letters I always wrote 'one day'. Is today that day? I don't know. But today I'm here.
ch07.it.ch07_s8_desk.l1: The practice books are still on the desk. On the edge of the top one, in small letters: 'Over? Not yet.'
journal.ch07.ch07_s8_coat: Three coats on the hooks. One nobody can bring themselves to take down. Or nobody has given up on.
ch07.it.ch07_s8_coat.l1: Three coats on the hooks. Kemal's work jacket, Defne's thin coat, Rıza's leather jacket. None of them has moved.
ch07.it.ch07_s8_coat.l2: In one pocket a bus ticket, in one a truck key, in one half a throat lozenge.
ch07.it.ch07_s8_phone.l1: Seven messages on the answering machine. Six from reporters. One from Mother Hayriye: 'Son, come for dinner. All of you. Whoever's left.'
ch07.s8f_01: The flat is too big. A home for three is too big for one; four rooms of silence.
ch07.s8f_02: Dad's shaving brush is still on the edge of the sink. I'm not moving it. If I move it, he'll really be gone.
ch07.s8f_03: Defne's door is ajar. I'm not closing it. If I close it, I'll never open it again.
ch07.s8f_04: I've had a key to this flat for thirty years. Kemal gave it to me: 'the door's always open,' he said. The door's open. There's nobody inside.
ch07.s8f_05: The phone rings at midnight. A number, a voice: 'We're gathering at the gate tomorrow at six. Will you come?' It's Selim.
ch07.s8f_05_v1: The phone rings at midnight. Zeynep: 'We're gathering at the gate tomorrow at six. I'm bringing Deniz. Will you come?'
ch05.s8g_01: Nevin's desk. One drawer is half open. Inside, a file: 'Demirtaş Logistics — delivery notes.'
ch05.s8g_01_v1: Smoke seeps under the door. On Nevin's desk a drawer is half open, a file inside: 'Demirtaş Logistics — delivery notes.'
ch05.s8g_02: Twenty barrels. 'Cleaning supplies.' Signed for by: N. But there's another note beside it: 'Next to cell 3. Night.'
ch05.s8g_r1: Four photos. Two are blurred because her hands are shaking. Two are sharp enough.
ch05.s8g_r2: Defne shuts the drawer. Paper can wait. Someone is coughing in the corridor.
ch05.s8g_10: (on the phone) Rıza. You've got the barrels, I know. Bring them back tonight and your debt's gone. All of it. The ledger's closed.
ch05.s8g_11: (on the phone) Nothing happened at the plant tonight, Rıza. Nothing will. And you didn't see anything. Your interest is frozen for a month. My gift.
ch05.s8g_12: A gift. A gift from Cevdet. Write this in your ledger too: the first time anyone refused a gift from you.
ch05.s8g_20: (whispering into the phone) Selim, are you asleep? I'm at the plant. There's someone inside. Don't come. Just… keep your phone on.
ch05.s8g_21: (sleepy) Boss? Okay. It's on. Zeynep woke up too, she's listening as well. Be careful, boss.
ch06.it.ch06_s8_clock.l1: The clock is four minutes fast. Nobody has corrected it. Even time is a little impatient in this room.
journal.ch06.ch06_s8_glass: A lip mark at the bottom of the tea glass in the interview room: somebody sat here before me and didn't finish their tea.
ch06.it.ch06_s8_glass.l1: Half a glass of tea at the edge of the table. Cold. A lip mark on the rim; someone sat here before you.
ch06.s8g_01: A woman in the corridor with a file and a wet umbrella. 'I'm from the union. Leyla Tan, lawyer.'
ch06.s8g_02: I don't know what you said in there, but whatever you said is now a statement on record. Now tell me. All of it, or part of it.
ch06.s8g_c1.all: All of it. The robot, the gate, the container, the envelope.
ch06.s8g_c1.part: Only what was asked. The rest is mine to carry.
ch06.s8g_c1.prompt: How much do you tell the lawyer?
ch06.s8g_r1: This is a heavy file. But heavy files sit well in court; the wind can't blow them away. There are cameras outside. Whatever you do, my name is next to yours.
ch06.s8g_r2: Everyone carries a part. The trouble is that the people carrying the parts don't know each other. There are cameras outside. It's your call.
ch06.s8g_03: Camera flashes show through the glass in the door. At the end of the corridor the exit sign blinks green.
